name: H2O-3 Architecture
description: H2O-3 is an open-source, distributed, in-memory machine learning platform designed for big data analytics. It uses a columnar compressed storage format and MapReduce-style distributed computing to train models on large datasets across clusters. Provides APIs for R, Python, Scala, and REST.

concept.distributedInMemory: Data stored compressed in-memory across cluster nodes
concept.columnarStorage: Data stored by columns for efficient compression and access
concept.h2oFrame: Distributed data frame (analogous to R/Pandas DataFrame)
concept.explanation: H2O distributes data across nodes in compressed columnar format. Algorithms execute in parallel using fork-join parallelism. Results aggregated across nodes.

idealScenarios: Large datasets that don't fit in single machine memory
Teams using multiple languages (R, Python, Java)

modeling.types: GLM, GBM, Random Forest, Deep Learning, K-Means, PCA, etc.

architectureLayers.restApi: JSON over HTTP for all operations
architectureLayers.storage: Optional integration with HDFS, S3, etc.

dataStructures.h2oFrame: 2D labeled data structure distributed across cluster
dataStructures.chunk: Subset of a column on a node

complexity.setup: Requires cluster setup or local H2O instance
complexity.memory: Data must fit in aggregate cluster memory
complexity.scalability: Scales linearly with nodes (for most algorithms)

cons: Less algorithmic depth than specialized libraries
